name: voxbox-vocal-channel
description: The canonical Manley VOXBOX use: a complete tube VOCAL channel in one pass — Mic-mode tube preamp (input 3 / gain 50, gentle even-harmonic warmth) with the 80 Hz low-cut engaged, the passive-opto compressor leveling the vocal (nominal 3:1, program-dependent, first in the chain; comp_thresh 9, Medium attack / Med Slow release = smooth, transparent ride that keeps articulation), the passive Pultec-style EQ adding chest/body (lo_peak 3 @100 Hz), de-honking the low-mids (mid_dip -3 @700 Hz) and opening air (hi_peak 5 @12 kHz), and the frequency-conscious de-esser taming sibilance (sel 6K, thr 8). This is a STARTING POINT tuned for lead vocals; the numbers were sanity-rendered on the Watercolors drum loop (it renders, crest ~19) but are meant for a dry vocal — set comp_thresh and de_ess_thr by ear/meter to the actual voice.
intended_for: lead/backing VOCALS — the box's reason to exist (tube pre -> ELOP -> Pultec EQ -> de-ess in one channel). Also a strong starting point for bass DI and acoustic guitar (drop the de-esser). Re-tune comp_thresh (GR) and de_ess_thr to the source level.
plugin_build: UADx 'uaudio_manley_voxbox.vst3' (UADx NATIVE — RENDERS headless via Pedalboard 0.9.23; NOT the 'UAD Manley VOXBOX.component' passthrough twin). 25 params, all enums; the string switches (source_select=Mic, low_cut='80 Hz', comp_byp/eq_byp/de_ess_byp=In, comp_attack/comp_rel, de_ess_sel, sc_link, transformer_byp) MUST go through this setattr harness — apply-vst-chain's float dict can't set them.
notes: TUNE TO THE VOICE. comp_thresh is RELATIVE TO INPUT — higher number = more GR. For a dry vocal at a sane level, start comp_thresh ~5-7 and watch the GR meter for ~3 dB on loud phrases (Manley/UA guidance: don't exceed ~-3 dB GR on tracking or it softens); raise `input` if it won't grab. The compressor is a smooth, program-dependent passive-opto (nominal 3:1) sitting FIRST in the chain (before the preamp) — Medium attack + Med Slow release keeps consonants intact while leveling the body. For a great singer, Slow attack + Slow release mimics fader-riding.

DE-ESS: de_ess_sel picks the detection band (6K is typical sibilance; 9K/12K for brighter mics, 3K for chesty/proximity / 'sounds that hurt'). It notches the DETECTOR (frequency-conscious — the whole signal ducks when the chosen band exceeds threshold). de_ess_thr higher = more ducking; measured it needs ~thr 8+ to act meaningfully and only acts where there's energy at that freq (~-1.8 dB @6k at thr 10). Set by the D-S meter / by ear; aim for natural, not removed. (The final 'Limit' position of the same knob is a smooth opto LA-2A-style wideband 10:1 limiter, NOT de-ess — see voxbox-bus-tube-glue.)

sc_link 'Link'/'Sep' is a STEREO L/R link (it links the two channels' compressor thresholds on a stereo source) — it is NOT a comp<->de-ess link. On a mono vocal it's moot (the plugin locks mono-in to Link); measured Sep == Link on this mono material. Left at 'Link' here for the mono/stereo default.

PULTEC EQ is passive and the 0-10 dials are nonlinear (the action is 5-10; under ~3 barely moves). lo_peak/hi_peak are boost BELLS, mid_dip a cut BELL. Classic vocal Pultec: lo_peak @100 for chest, hi_peak @10-16k for air, mid_dip @500-1k to de-box/de-honk.
low_cut '80 Hz' (or '120 Hz') is the input HPF — engage it on close vocals to drop rumble/proximity before the preamp.
Harness peak-normalizes to -1 dBFS (absorbs the Mic-mode level). Set dump_state=true via apply-vst-chain once dialed for a byte-stable re-render.
